pr.title: Tidy the update view
pr.body: Small cleanup in `blog.update`; no behavior change intended.
pr.bug: Edits are never committed: the redirect succeeds but the post keeps its old title and body.

findings.label: regression
findings.why: Removing db.commit() prevents the UPDATE from being persisted, so the post retains its old title and body instead of the new values.

findings.label: regression
findings.why: Removing db.commit() prevents the UPDATE from being persisted, so the post retains its old title and body instead of the new values.

doppel.summary: The PR removes the commit call, causing updates to not be saved — a regression despite the 'no behavior change intended' claim.

suspicions.claim: Removing db.commit() causes the UPDATE transaction to be rolled back at request teardown, so the post title/body are not persisted.
suspicions.trigger: 1. Log in as alice (POST /auth/login username=alice password=doppel-pass). 2. POST /1/update with form title=NewTitle body=NewBody. 3. Follow redirect to GET /. 4. Check that the post with id=1 still shows the old title/body (or query DB directly: SELECT title, body FROM post WHERE id=1).
suspicions.evidence: Probe probe_s1 sent POST /1/update with title=NewTitle body=NewBody; base responded with updated title/body (NewTitle, NewBody) on the update page and index, while head responded with the original title/body (First Post, This is the first post.) on both pages, showing the UPDATE was rolled back in head.

review.why: The PR removes the `db.commit()` call after the UPDATE statement in the `update` view, so changes to a post will not be persisted to the database.
